subject: Pricing for Insights product launch — incremental commit vs per-token tiers
messages:
From: Aleksei Moroz <aleksei@finlytics.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finlytics.ai; marta@finlytics.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing for new product launch — incremental commit vs per-token scaling

Hi Sergio,

Quick note from the Insights team — we’re spinning up a new summarization product (internal team name: Insights) that will hit production in Q2. Estimated incremental Hosted API usage for the new endpoint is ~600M tokens/month initially, ramping to ~1.5B within 6 months if early tests are positive.

Questions we need to nail down from pricing/procurement:
- Do you offer a per-token tiered discount schedule for hosted API usage? If so, what are the thresholds and effective unit prices?
- Alternatively, can we do an incremental commit (credits) that applies across multiple products/teams? If we commit to X tokens/month for 12 months, how do you treat new workloads that come online mid-term?
- Is there any onboarding credit or promotional uplift for first-quarter volume?
- Region: we need all traffic routed through us-west.

Procurement attached a simple usage_estimate.xlsx for FY27 Q2/Q3 to give you visibility.

We’re hoping to finalize commercial approach and timeline (SOW/MA + DocuSign) within two weeks. Can you outline options so we can share with finance?

Thanks — Aleksei
Aleksei Moroz
Head of Product, Insights
Finlytics AI

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com; neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Pricing for new product launch — incremental commit vs per-token scaling

Aleksei — thanks for the context and the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. High-level options (hosted API):

1) Tiered per-token pricing (no commit) — simple and flexible:
   - 0–500M tokens/month: list price
   - 500M–2B tokens/month: ~10% unit discount off list
   - 2B+ tokens/month: ~18% unit discount off list
   - Billing monthly, no minimum term.

2) Incremental commit (preferred for predictable spend):
   - Example: 250M token/month committed credit -> equivalent to ~12% blended discount vs list for workloads covered by the commit.
   - Commits can be applied across multiple products/teams under the same legal entity; you designate which workloads count toward the commit.
   - True-up at quarter end; unused credits can be rolled forward for one quarter or refunded at a reduced rate (depends on term).
   - Term: typically 12 months for meaningful pricing; 6 months possible for pilots but with smaller discounts.

3) Short-term promotional uplift (pilot):
   - We can offer a one-time promotional credit equal to ~5% of the first month’s billed tokens for new workloads if you sign a 6-month pilot commit.

Recommended path for Finlytics: start with a 6-month pilot commit for the Insights team (250–500M/month) with a conversion clause to a 12-month commit if you hit 1B/month within 3 months. That gives you price predictability while keeping flexibility for other teams to onboard.

Next steps I suggest: I’ll pull together a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a commercial summary (MA + SOW template). Can you confirm:
- Final billing entity name and PO process?
- Is procurement fine with monthly billing + quarterly true-up?
- Any required contract language for data residency / us-west routing?

I’m attaching our standard MA template for procurement to review.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com; neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for new product launch — internal note

Laura / Neha — looping you in for quick alignment. Finlytics is looking at 600M/month initially for Insights; procurement will likely push for a single-year committed credit that covers multiple teams. My proposal:

- Offer a 12-month commit at 300M/month as baseline (converts to a 15% effective discount for workloads covered).
- Add ramp clause: if usage exceeds 1B/month for the combined account within the first 90 days, automatic repricing to the next discount band (reduce net unit price by additional 3%).
- Promotional concession: first 2 months of trial usage outside the commit are eligible for a 50% credit applied to the next invoice only if they sign the 12-month term within 30 days.

Trade-offs: the promotional concession is slightly aggressive; we should cap absolute credit exposure at $40k. Finance OK with that cap? If so I’ll include in the MA and present to procurement.

Sergio

Thanks, Sergio — that was helpful. Procurement reviewed the MA template and has two items before we proceed:
1) They prefer a single committed-credit purchase for year 1 that can be reallocated across teams by admin (we can provide a list of workloads that will be covered after signature).
2) They want monthly billing with a 30-day invoice payment term; any true-up should be on a quarterly cadence.

Also: do you require Reserved/Dedicated capacity for predictable latency at 1–1.5B tokens/month? Or can Hosted API with the commitment handle SLA needs? If capacity/latency constraints require Dedicated, procurement will need a quote for Dedicated pools and lead time.

I attached a draft SOW to accelerate alignment. Can you send a consolidated commercial summary and a DocuSign link so procurement can start the approval flow?

Best —
Aleksei

Aleksei / Procurement team — attaching a consolidated commercial summary and the DocuSign envelope to start signatures. Summary of proposed commercials:

- Billing entity: Finlytics AI, Inc.
- Offer: 12-month committed credit, 300M tokens/month (baseline) -> blended ~15% discount vs list for covered workloads.
- True-up: quarterly true-up; monthly billing, 30-day net payment terms.
- Ramp clause: automatic repricing to the next band if combined usage >1B/month for 2 consecutive months.
- Pilot concession: credits for first 2 months (capped at $40k) if contract signed within 30 days.
- Region/data residency: Hosted API endpoints pinned to us-west; redwood to provide routing SLA in MA.
- Dedicated capacity: not required at baseline; we’ll monitor latency for first 90 days and provide Dedicated quote if observed p50/p95 exceed agreed thresholds.
